a:r.a:t: Polyketides Are Biologically Active Lipids with Medicinal Uses
Polyketides are a diverse family of compounds synthesized similarly to fatty acid biosynthesis.
commonly secondary metabolites with specialized function

p:cNvPr.descr: The complex structures of three polyketide compounds. On the left is erythromycin (labeled below). It consists of 2 ring structures on the right and a large, 16-sided component on the right. The large 16-sided component is double bonded to O at the top. This C bonds down and left to C, which bonds left to a solid wedge and down to C, which solid wedge bonds right (into the structure) to OH. This C bonds down and left to C, which solid wedge bonds up and left to OH, with a dashed wedge bond pointing down and left. The C then bonds straight down to the next C, which has a dashed wedge bond connected to a straight line bond down and to the left. C then bonds down and right to O, which is part of the ring. O bonds right to C, which double bonds down & left to O, and right to C, which has solid wedge bond pointing down. This C bonds up and right to C, which dashed wedge bonds right to O. C then bonds straight up to C, which dashed wedge bonds left, into the structure. C then bonds up and right to C, which dashed wedge bonds right to O and up to C, which solid wedge bonds up to OH and dashed wedge bonds right. The C then bonds up and left to C, which bonds straight up to C. This C has a dashed wedge bond to its upper right, and it bonds up and left to C, which double bonds up to O. This is our starting point. Now, the upper dashed wedge bonded O on the right side of the structure bonds right to a tetrahyropyran (6-sided ring containing an O) viewed in the chair configuration. The O bonds right to C, which bonds out to H and to the next C, which makes a sharp left and bonds to C, which bonds up to N(CH3)2, then left to C, which bonds angled out to OH. This C then bonds to the C bonded left to the O. The large structure has another wedge-bonded O below this one; it bonds right to another tetrahydropyran ring. The O in the ring bonds right to C, which bonds angled to H and right to C. C bonds up & right to OH, and makes a sharp left to C, which bonds up to OH and angled down to H. This C bonds left to C, which bonds left to C and up to O, where it is connected to the main part of the compound. On the right is amphotericin B (antifungal) (labeled below). It consists of 2 parallel connected carbon chains with various substituents. Beginning from the carbon on the left bottom side of the molecule, to the right there is a 15-carbon chain where every other bond is a double bond. On the 15th carbon in the chain, C solid wedge bonds down to O, bonds up to C, which bonds up to C again. This C bonds up to C, which bonds left to O and up to C. This C solid wedge bonds down & right to C, which double bonds up to O and down to OH (a carbonyl group). Back on the chain, C bonds up to C, which dashed wedge bonds up & right to OH. C bonds up and left to C, which bonds down and left to C, which solid wedge bonds up to OH and down to O, which bonds to the O that is already connected to the C earlier in the chain. This O actually forms a tetrahydropyran ring within the larger structure. The carbon to which this is bonded bonds left to C. Here begins an 11-carbon stretch where there are only a total of 5 solid wedge bonded OH, 4 below the chain and 1 above the chain. All the way at the leftmost end, C double bonds down to O and up & left to O. O bonds down and left to C, which has a dashed wedge bond to the left and bonds down to C, which has a dashed wedge bond to the right. The C then bonds left and down to C, which has a solid wedge bond up and left to OH. This C bonds down to C, which has a dashed wedge bond going down & left. Now we are back at the initial carbon chain (the bottom chain). The final compound, below the other two, is lovastatin (statin) (labeled below). The bottom of the structure contains 2 cyclohexane rings, each with a double bond at the bottom right side of the ring. The leftmost ring has a dashed wedge bond on its lower left C. At the top of this ring, the C dashed wedge bonds up to O. O bonds up and left to C, which double bonds up to O, down and left to C, which has a solid wedge bond down and which bonds left to C, which in turn bonds left to C again. To the right, between the two rings, there is a solid wedge bond oriented straight upward. The ring to the right has a solid wedge bond on its upper right corner. To the left of this, the ring's topmost C dashed wedge bonds up & right to H, and solid wedge bonds straight up to C, which bonds right to C. C dashed wedge bonds up to C, which solid wedge bonds down and right to H and up to a tetrahydropyran (6-sided ring with 1 O). The O is at the bottom right. O is double bonded at the top right side of the ring; OH is solid wedge bonded to the top left side of the ring.
